title: cohort-based-multi-gpu-serving-heuristics
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a pragmatic design direction and experiment plan for coordinating kernels, pipeline fragments, and KV cache shards across many GPUs using a cohort-based scheduling model. The intent is not to replace the existing NCCL-first tuning docs, but to offer an orthogonal approach that: 1) reduces small-batch tail latency for heterogenous sequences, 2) minimizes expensive cross-node collectives under load, and 3) gracefully degrades to cheaper single-GPU execution when fragmentation is severe.

Background / motivation:
- Production workloads show a long tail driven by mixed sequence lengths (8 to 4096 tokens), I/O jitter from downstream tooling (client-side backoff), and variable KV reuse. Our current per-request placement strategy can cause partial kernel stalls, frequent small collectives, or suboptimal memory utilization when serving multi-tenant workloads.
- Anecdotal ops notes: some Dedicated clusters see 12-18% extra token-cost due to repeated small inter-GPU collectives at high QPS.

Key idea: cohorts and execution quantum
- Cohort: a small set of concurrently executing requests that the runtime groups for coordinated dispatch and kernel alignment. Cohorts are formed transiently (20-200ms window) rather than permanently pinned. They are sized by a heuristic: {min_batch_for_collective, max_latency_budget, memory_headroom}.
- Quantum: a scheduling epoch (micro-time slice) during which kernel scheduling, KV coalescing, and collective invocation decisions are made. Typical quantum values to try: 8ms, 16ms, 32ms.
- By aligning requests into cohorts, we increase the probability of creating collective-friendly batches (larger, same-phase microbatches) without adding an explicit batching delay per-request.

Cohort formation heuristics (initial proposal)
1) Eligibility: requests eligible for cohorting must be stateless generation or short-lived chat reads (i.e., no long synchronous tool calls pending).
2) Signal sources: sequence length estimate, cached-prefix-hit boolean, model-variant affinity, originating tenant QoS tier, and request arrival jitter (inter-arrival delta).
3) Priority scoring: score = w1*prefetchable + w2*len_similarity + w3*tenant_weight - w4*est_fulfillment_latency. Tunable weights to start: w1=3, w2=1.5, w3=1.0, w4=2.0.
4) Size cap: cohort size = min( ceil(memory_headroom / avg_req_size), configured_max_cohort ), with configured_max_cohort=48 as a starting point.

Kernel coordination model
- Kernel handshake: before launching a multi-GPU kernel that will engage in collectives, shards participating in the cohort exchange a tiny control message (sub-ms) to confirm readiness and memory layout. This handshake allows dynamic switching between collective-mode and local-mode to avoid expensive synchronizations if a participant lags.
- Fallbacks: if handshake fails for >25% participants within quantum, fallback to local execution variant (replicated or intra-GPU tiling).
- Stitching fragments: support chunked-kernel execution where a partially finished kernel can hand off KV cache pointers and microbatch offsets to a second kernel without re-copying activations (in-memory pointer stitching). This reduces PCIe transfers in host-offload designs.

KV shard coalescing and lifespan policies
- Soft coalescing: merge small KV shards from a cohort into a temporary contiguous allocation for the duration of the cohort to reduce fragmented DMA and remote reads. This lives in a per-GPU transient arena and is freed after cohort eviction.
- Lifespan heuristics: prefer coalescing if estimated read-count > 2 in the next 150ms. If read-count low, avoid to reduce allocation churn.
- Eviction policy: cohort-coalesced shards have lower priority vs pinned model shards; eviction is LRU within the transient arena.

Collective strategy and NCCL tuning knobs (experimental)
- Collective batching: prefer fewer, larger collectives over many small ones. Define collective threshold by tokens_in_flight >= T_collective where T_collective is tunable (start 1024 tokens).
- NCCL parameters to test: NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0/1, NCCL_ALGO=RING/Tree, NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS, NCCL_BUFFSIZE. The runtime should expose a per-cluster profile that can switch between ring-optimized and tree-optimized for low-latency vs high-throughput workloads.
- Async collective mode: when cohort quantum large enough (>16ms) and participants span nodes, issue non-blocking collectives and allow local progress via dedicated progress threads pinned to spare cores.

Placement and shard orchestration heuristics
- Prefer intra-node cohorts when memory headroom and network topologies favor it (reduces NVLink/P2P contention). Use simple topology-awareness: prefer GPUs that share NVLink switches; fall back to cross-node only when intra-node cannot satisfy cohort memory/compute needs.
- Shard coalescing across nodes only if (expected collective savings > estimated cross-node transfer cost + extra latency). Estimate cross-node transfer cost via recent p95 ping + bandwidth model.

Microbenchmark plan
- Benchmarks to run: short-chat (8-64 tokens), mixed-length streaming (8-512 tokens), long-generation (1024-4096 tokens), and KV-heavy prefix reuse traces from production (sampled).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, host CPU utilization, NCCL collective efficiency (bytes/sec and latency per collective), transient arena allocation churn, and observed fallback rate (handshake failures).
- Baseline runs: current per-request placement; optimized runs: cohort quantum=8/16/32ms, cohort_size caps 16/32/48, collective threshold 512/1024/2048 tokens.

Operational signals and observability
- Add per-cohort telemetry: cohort_id, formation_time, size, participants (gpu ids), quantum_value, handshake_success_fraction, collectives_emitted, total_tokens, coalesced_bytes, fallback_reason (if any).
- Alerting heuristics: if cohort fallback_rate > 10% sustained for 5m and p95 latency increases >15% vs baseline, raise a perf-regression incident.

Risks and failure modes
- Head-of-line blocking: cohorting might introduce additional latency for stragglers when cohort windows are misconfigured. Mitigation: aggressive fast-path for high-priority tenants (bypass cohorting) and adaptive quantum shrink on high tail.
- Memory churn: transient arena allocations could increase OOM risk in high-concurrency clusters. Mitigation: hard caps, and immediate fallback to non-coalesced execution if arena usage > X% (start X=60%).
- Complexity of handshake: poorly engineered handshake can add overhead that negates gains. Keep handshake minimal (8-16 bytes) and time-bounded.

Open questions / discussion items
- How to integrate with existing rollout policies (canary/A-B) in Console? Need a per-cluster toggle and a flag to set cohort_quantum and collective thresholds per rollout.
- Can we derive sequence length estimates cheaply on first token for better cohort matching without doing a full tokenization? Ideas: client hints, rough token_count header, or early-token prediction models.
- Should cohort eligibility be tenant-configurable (some customers may want strict single-request isolation)?

Next steps and immediate TODOs
- Implement lightweight cohort controller prototype in runtime v0.1 (Ethan) with configurable quantum and simple scoring.
- Wire transient arena allocator and KV coalescing API (Lina).
- Add NCCL profile toggles and a microbenchmark harness that collects collective-level metrics (Noah).
- Run first experiments against prod-sampled traces, compare against baseline (target by 2026-03-01).

Notes to reviewers:
- This document is intentionally pragmatic and experiment-focused. I expect a few iterations of the scoring weights and quantum choices after first-run telemetry. Focus review on the failure modes and the minimal handshake semantics — we should keep that interface tiny and deterministic.
